facebook.long_form:

Paul George made sure everyone remembered why he left Philadelphia.

The Boston Celtics star returned to the Wells Fargo Center on Tuesday night and put on an absolute show — 36 points, six three-pointers, in a 123-101 Boston victory. Jayson Tatum added 21 as the Celtics dismantled a Philadelphia squad that simply had no answer for their former player in full revenge-game mode.

There's always extra electricity when a player faces his old team for the first time. George channeled every bit of that energy. Whether the crowd's reaction fueled him or it was pure competitive focus, the result was the same: a clinic from one of the NBA's premier scorers.

The Celtics pick up an important road win and serve notice that they are very much a contender in the Eastern Conference.

What's your take — was this Paul George's best game as a Celtic so far? 👇

Brunson 23. KAT 21 and 16 boards. Knicks WIN their FOURTH STRAIGHT, 117-85. New York is rolling. #Knicks #NBA

Character count: 108 ✓

facebook.long_form:
Posting window: 9:00 AM ET

The New York Knicks are playing their best basketball of the season — and the Milwaukee Bucks are having a nightmare start.

New York cruised to a 117-85 win on Tuesday night behind Jalen Brunson's 23 points and Karl-Anthony Towns' double-double of 21 points and 16 rebounds. It was the Knicks' fourth consecutive victory, and they look increasingly dangerous.

Meanwhile, Milwaukee dropped to 1-10 with their seventh straight loss. For a Bucks team with the talent to compete deep into the playoffs, this start is alarming. Something is simply not clicking in Milwaukee — whether it's chemistry, scheme, or the weight of expectations, the holes in their game are being exposed every night.

Can the Bucks turn this around? The season is young, but the losses are piling up fast.

A 1-10 record. Seven straight losses. The Milwaukee Bucks' season is at a crossroads, and it's only early November.

This is a team built to compete at the highest level, and yet something is deeply wrong right now. Losses are mounting, confidence appears shaken, and opponents are exploiting their weaknesses relentlessly.

History tells us that some teams recover from poor starts to make deep playoff runs. It also tells us that for every miraculous turnaround, there are three teams that never find their footing. The window for recovery is not unlimited.

The Bucks have the talent. Do they have the resolve? The next two weeks will tell us a lot.
